headline: Bialecki finally cracks Price at Minehead
standfirst: Gerwyn Price had beaten Sebastian Bialecki all six times they had met. The Grand Slam champion's seventh try ended 6-4 to the Pole.
body: Gerwyn Price arrived at Butlins as the Grand Slam champion and a man who had never lost to Sebastian Bialecki. By the end of Friday night both of those things were old news. Bialecki, ranked 42nd, beat the world number three 6-4.

The averages tell you how close it was: 95.61 to 95.54. Price is usually a 98.63 man over 12 months, so this was a quiet night for him, and Bialecki, a 92.74 player on that measure, played above himself. Bialecki led from the first leg and was 4-2 ahead before Price started to claw back. A 120 finish in the ninth leg made it 5-4 and left Price one leg from a decider.

He never got it. Bialecki had the throw for the tenth leg and finished it on double seven after 17 darts. Neither player was brilliant on the doubles, Bialecki hitting 37.5 per cent to Price's 40, but Price did not make a single break of throw all night.
Bialecki goes into the last 32 on Saturday against Jeffrey De Graaf, who knocked out Gian van Veen in the same session. Price goes home with £4,000 and a fresh sense of how fast a title run can fade.
Our view: Bialecki has now got over the mental block, and that makes him dangerous for the next month.
